summary: This work presents analytical calculations of surface barriers and RF surface resistance in superconducting multilayer structures for SRF cavity applications, comparing conventional materials (NbN, Nb$_3$Sn) with iron-based superconductors (FeSe). Simultaneous optimization of vortex penetration field $B_v$ and surface resistance $R_s$ is proposed as a design strategy, with FeSe/I/Nb$_3$Sn achieving $B_v = 508.3$ mT and ultra-low $R_s = 9.31 \times 10^{-3}$ nΩ compared to bulk Nb's $B_v = 180$ mT and $R_s = 22.26$ nΩ.
motivation: Bulk niobium SRF cavities approach their performance limits, and operation above 4 K requires materials with larger superconducting gaps; multilayer structures can enhance critical fields via the Bean-Livingston barrier while iron-based superconductors offer both larger gaps and lower normal-state conductivity $\sigma_0$ to reduce RF losses.
method: Analytical multilayer theory solving London and Maxwell equations determines magnetic and electric field distributions in S/I/S structures; vortex penetration fields and surface resistance (via Mattis-Bardeen theory for $s$-wave and phenomenological $s^{\pm}$-wave models for iron-pnictides) are calculated as functions of layer thicknesses $d_S$ and $d_I$ at $T = 2$ K and $\nu = 1.3$ GHz.
result: Nb$_3$Sn/I/Nb achieves optimal performance on Nb substrates ($B_v = 480.8$ mT, $R_s = 3.09$ nΩ), while FeSe/I/Nb matches this ($B_v = 370$ mT, $R_s = 5.35$ nΩ) with superior mechanical properties; remarkably, substrate contribution dominates surface resistance, inverting conventional optimization priorities.
